Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their wives, and what they used to worship﴾ ﴿besides Allah, and lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾ ﴿and stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ ﴿Rather, today they are submitting﴾ ﴿and they turn to one another, questioning each other﴾.

There are several discussions concerning the verse.

The First Discussion: Know that there is no dispute that this is part of the speech of the angels. If it is asked: what is the meaning of ﴿gather﴾, since they had already been gathered earlier, were present at the assembly of the Resurrection, and said ﴿This is the Day of Judgment﴾, and the angels said to them ﴿This is the Day of Decision﴾? al-Qadi answered this, saying: the meaning is "gather them to the abode of recompense, which is the Fire." That is why He says after it ﴿and lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾, i.e., "take them along that road and guide them to it." Then he asked himself: how is that valid, when He says after it ﴿and stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾, and it is known that their being gathered to Hellfire happens only after the questioning? He answered that in a conjunction with the particle "wa" (and) there is no indication of sequence, so there is no obstacle to saying "gather them and stop them," even though we know by reason that the stopping occurred before the gathering to the Fire. This is what al-Qadi said. In my view there is another possibility, namely that it may be said: when they rise from their graves, it is not unlikely that they stop there in bewilderment that overtakes them because of witnessing the terrors of the Resurrection. Then Allah, exalted is He, says to the angels: "Gather those who did wrong and lead them to the path of Hellfire," i.e., drive them to the road of Hell and stop them there; the questioning takes place there, and then from there they are driven to the Fire. According to this interpretation, the apparent wording of the text agrees with what this view holds.

The Second Discussion: The one giving the command in His saying ﴿You used to deny﴾ and ﴿Gather those who did wrong﴾ is Allah. So He, exalted is He, commanded the angels to gather the disbelievers to the place of questioning, and by "gathering" is meant that the angels drive them to that place.

The Third Discussion: Allah commanded the angels to gather three things: the wrongdoers, their wives, and the things they used to worship. In this there are several benefits.

The First Benefit: He, exalted is He, said ﴿Gather those who did wrong﴾, then He mentioned among the attributes of "those who did wrong" that they worshipped other than Allah. This indicates that the absolute wrongdoer is the disbeliever, and this shows that every threat that came concerning the wrongdoer is directed toward the disbelievers. What confirms this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ (2:254).

The Second Benefit: They differed about what is meant by "their wives," and there are three opinions.

The first: by "their wives" is meant their likenesses, i.e., their companions and their peers in disbelief. So the Jew is with the Jew, and the Christian with the Christian. The following points indicate that "wives" may mean likenesses:

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you were in three kinds﴾ (56:7), i.e., types and likenesses.

The second: you say, "I have pairs of this," meaning equals, and you say, "a pair of shoes," because each one is the counterpart of the other. Likewise, a man and a woman are called a pair (zawjayn) because they are alike in most rules of marriage. Likewise, the even number is called by this name because each of its two halves is an example of the second part in whole numbers. Al-Wahidi said: according to this opinion, "those who did wrong" must mean the leaders, because if you took "those who did wrong" to be general, covering everyone who associated partners with Allah, then "wives" would have no meaning.

The second opinion regarding the interpretation of "wives" is that what is meant is their companions among the devils, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And their brothers aid them in error, then they do not stop﴾ (7:202).

The third opinion is that what is meant is their women who were upon their religion. As for His saying ﴿and what they used to worship﴾ ﴿besides Allah﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: what is meant is what they used to worship besides Allah, of idols and tyrannical powers. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿So beware of the Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ (2:24). It has been said: by "men" is meant the worshippers of idols, and by "stones" is meant the idols, which are carved stones. If it is asked: those stones are inanimate, so what is the benefit of gathering them to Hell? al-Qadi answered: a report has come that they will be brought back and will come to life, so that the rebuke of the disbelievers who worshipped them may be intensified. But someone may say: suppose Allah brings those idols to life, still no sin proceeded from them, so how is it permissible for Allah to punish them? The closer view is to say that Allah does not bring those idols to life, but leaves them in their inanimateness, and then casts them into Hell, because that increases the disbelievers' shame.

The second opinion: what is meant by His saying ﴿and what they used to worship﴾ ﴿besides Allah﴾ is the devils who invited them to worship what they worshipped. When they accepted that religion from them, they became like worshippers of those devils. This is confirmed by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan?﴾ (36:60). The first opinion is preferable, because the devils are rational beings, and the word "ma" (what) does not suit rational beings. And Allah knows best.

Then He said: ﴿So lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Guide them," meaning "show them the way." One says, "I guided the man" when you showed him the way. The word "guidance" (hidayah) is used here because it is put in place of guidance to Paradise, as He said: ﴿So give them the good news of a painful punishment﴾ (3:21). So the "good news" of punishment befalls these people in place of the good news of bliss for those others. It is also reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿so guide them﴾ means "drive them." Al-Asamm said: it means "send them forward." Al-Wahidi said: this is a mistake, because "hada" is said when one goes ahead, and from it come "al-hidayah" (guidance), "al-hawadi," and "al-hadiyat" (wild animals that go ahead of the herd). He said: "hada" is not said with the meaning of "sent forward." Then he said: ﴿and stop them﴾. One says, "I stopped the riding animal, I stop it, a stopping (waqf), and it stopped, stopping (wuqufan)," and the meaning is "hold them back." In the verse there are two opinions:

One of them: there is a transposition, and the meaning is "stop them and guide them." The more correct view is that there is no need for this. Rather, it is as if it were said: ﴿So lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾, and when they reach the path, it is said: ﴿and stop them﴾, for the questioning takes place there. As for His saying ﴿for they are to be questioned﴾, it has been said: about their deeds in the world and their statements. It is permissible that this questioning is what is mentioned after it, namely His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾, meaning they are questioned as a rebuke to them, and it is said: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Not one of you helps another as you used to in the world." That is because Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "We are a united host, invincible," so it was said to them on the Day of Resurrection: "What is the matter with you, not helping one another?" It has also been said: it is said to the disbelievers, "What is the matter with your partners that they do not protect you from the punishment?"

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you were in three kinds﴾ (56:7), i.e., types and likenesses.

Likewise, the even number is called by this name because each of its two halves is an example of the second part in whole numbers. Then He said: ﴿So lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Guide them," meaning "show them the way." One says, "I guided the man" when you showed him the way. Al-Asamm said: it means "send them forward." Al-Wahidi said: this is a mistake, because "hada" is said when one goes ahead, and from it come "al-hidayah" (guidance), "al-hawadi," and "al-hadiyat" (wild animals that go ahead of the herd). He said: "hada" is not said with the meaning of "sent forward." Then he said: ﴿and stop them﴾. One says, "I stopped the riding animal, I stop it, a stopping (waqf), and it stopped, stopping (wuqufan)," and the meaning is "hold them back." In the verse there are two opinions:

Rather, it is as if it were said: ﴿So lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾, and when they reach the path, it is said: ﴿and stop them﴾, for the questioning takes place there. It has also been said: what is meant is that the guardians of Hell question them: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ They say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come true against the disbelievers" (39:71). That is because Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "We are a united host, invincible," so it was said to them on the Day of Resurrection: "What is the matter with you, not helping one another?" It has also been said: it is said to the disbelievers, "What is the matter with your partners that they do not protect you from the punishment?"

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, today they are submitting﴾. One says "istaslama lil-shay'" when he yields to a thing and submits to it. Its original meaning is seeking safety by abandoning dispute. The intended sense is that they have become compliant, having no means of warding off those harms, neither the worshipper nor the worshipped.

* * *

They say, "You deceived us," and those say, "Why did you accept from us?" In sum, that is not the questioning of those seeking information, but rather the questioning of rebuke and blame. And Allah knows best.

The second opinion regarding the interpretation of "wives" is that what is meant is their companions among the devils, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And their brothers aid them in error, then they do not stop﴾ (7:202).

The third opinion is that what is meant is their women who were upon their religion. As for His saying ﴿and what they used to worship﴾ ﴿besides Allah﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: what is meant is what they used to worship besides Allah, of idols and tyrannical powers. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿So beware of the Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ (2:24). It has been said: by "men" is meant the worshippers of idols, and by "stones" is meant the idols, which are carved stones. If it is asked: those stones are inanimate, so what is the benefit of gathering them to Hell? al-Qadi answered: a report has come that they will be brought back and will come to life, so that the rebuke of the disbelievers who worshipped them may be intensified. But someone may say: suppose Allah brings those idols to life, still no sin proceeded from them, so how is it permissible for Allah to punish them? The closer view is to say that Allah does not bring those idols to life, but leaves them in their inanimateness, and then casts them into Hell, because that increases the disbelievers' shame.

The second opinion: what is meant by His saying ﴿and what they used to worship﴾ ﴿besides Allah﴾ is the devils who invited them to worship what they worshipped. When they accepted that religion from them, they became like worshippers of those devils. This is confirmed by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan?﴾ (36:60). The first opinion is preferable, because the devils are rational beings, and the word "ma" (what) does not suit rational beings. And Allah knows best.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿So lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "Guide them," meaning "show them the way." One says, "I guided the man" when you showed him the way. The word "guidance" (hidayah) is used here because it is put in place of guidance to Paradise, as He said: ﴿So give them the good news of a painful punishment﴾ (3:21). So the "good news" of punishment befalls these people in place of the good news of bliss for those others. It is also reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿so guide them﴾ means "drive them." Al-Asamm said: it means "send them forward." Al-Wahidi said: this is a mistake, because "hada" is said when one goes ahead, and from it come "al-hidayah" (guidance), "al-hawadi," and "al-hadiyat" (wild animals that go ahead of the herd). He said: "hada" is not said with the meaning of "sent forward." Then he said: ﴿and stop them﴾. One says, "I stopped the riding animal, I stop it, a stopping (waqf), and it stopped, stopping (wuqufan)," and the meaning is "hold them back." In the verse there are two opinions:

One of them: there is a transposition, and the meaning is "stop them and guide them." The more correct view is that there is no need for this. Rather, it is as if it were said: ﴿So lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾, and when they reach the path, it is said: ﴿and stop them﴾, for the questioning takes place there. As for His saying ﴿for they are to be questioned﴾, it has been said: about their deeds in the world and their statements. It has also been said: what is meant is that the guardians of Hell question them: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ They say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come true against the disbelievers" (39:71). It is permissible that this questioning is what is mentioned after it, namely His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾, meaning they are questioned as a rebuke to them, and it is said: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Not one of you helps another as you used to in the world." That is because Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "We are a united host, invincible," so it was said to them on the Day of Resurrection: "What is the matter with you, not helping one another?" It has also been said: it is said to the disbelievers, "What is the matter with your partners that they do not protect you from the punishment?"

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, today they are submitting﴾. One says "istaslama lil-shay'" when he yields to a thing and submits to it. Its original meaning is seeking safety by abandoning dispute. The intended sense is that they have become compliant, having no means of warding off those harms, neither the worshipper nor the worshipped.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and they turn to one another﴾. It has been said: they are the people and the devils; it has also been said: the leaders and the followers.
﴿questioning each other﴾, i.e., some of them ask others. This questioning is an expression for mutual accusation, and it is a questioning of reproach. They say, "You deceived us," and those say, "Why did you accept from us?" In sum, that is not the questioning of those seeking information, but rather the questioning of rebuke and blame. And Allah knows best.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They will say, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right."﴾ ﴿They will say, "Rather, you were not believers."﴾ ﴿And we had no authority over you. Rather, you were a rebellious people.﴾ ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us: indeed, we are going to taste [the punishment].﴾ ﴿So we led you astray; indeed, we were ourselves astray.﴾ ﴿So on that Day they will be sharing in the punishment.﴾ ﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals.﴾ ﴿Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they would be arrogant.﴾ ﴿And they would say, "Are we to abandon our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, you are going to taste the painful punishment.﴾ ﴿And you are being recompensed only for what you used to do.﴾ ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah.﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, related that some of them would turn toward others, questioning one another, He explained the manner of that questioning. They said: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right.﴾ This is the statement of the followers to those who invited them to misguidance. Regarding the interpretation (tafsir, explanation) of "the right" (al-yamin) there are several aspects:

The first: the word "the right" here is a metaphor (isti'arah) for good things and felicities. The explanation of how this metaphor works is that the right side is superior to the left side, for several reasons:

One of them: all agree that the nobler of the two sides is the right.

The second: they do not undertake noble actions except with the right hand, such as shaking hands with the righteous, eating and drinking, whereas the opposite of these they do with the left hand.

The third: they used to seek omens of good luck, and they would consider the right side auspicious and call it "al-barih."

The fourth: the Prophet (ﷺ) loved to start with the right in everything.

The fifth: the Sharia ruled that the right side belongs to the recorder of good deeds and the left to the recorder of bad deeds.

The sixth: Allah, exalted is He, promised that the doer of good would be given his record in his right hand, and the doer of evil in his left hand. Thus it is established that the right side is superior to the left. Since this is so, it is inevitably the case that the word "right" is borrowed for good things, good deeds and acts of obedience. So His statement, ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right,﴾ means: you used to deceive us and give us the impression that your purpose in calling us to those religions was to support the truth and strengthen what is right.

The second aspect of interpretation: it is said, "So-and-so is the right [hand] of so-and-so" when he holds a good position with him. So these disbelievers said to their leaders, who had misled them and made disbelief attractive to them: you used to deceive us and give us the impression that we held a position of the right with you, that is, a good position, so we trusted you and accepted from you.

The third aspect: the leaders of disbelief had sworn to these weak ones that what they were calling them to was the truth. So they trusted their oaths and held to their covenants which they had made with them. Thus the meaning of His statement, ﴿you used to come to us from the right,﴾ is: from the direction of the pledges and oaths which you had given us.

The fourth aspect: the word "the right" is borrowed from strength and dominance, because the right hand is characterized by force, and it is with it that seizing occurs. The meaning is: you used to come to us from strength and dominance, and you aimed at us through authority and superiority, until you compelled us toward error and reproached us for it.

Then Allah, exalted is He, related that the leaders replied to the followers in several ways:

The first: they said to them, ﴿Rather, you were not believers,﴾ meaning: you were never characterized by faith such that it could be said that we removed you from it.

The second: their statement, ﴿And we had no authority over you,﴾ meaning: we had no power over you to overpower and compel you.

The third: ﴿Rather, you were a rebellious people,﴾ that is, you were going astray and exceeding the bounds in disobedience to Allah.

The fourth: their statement, ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us: indeed, we are going to taste [the punishment].﴾

Page 118

The meaning is that when Allah, exalted is He, informed of our falling into punishment, if our falling into punishment had not occurred, Allah's report would not have been true, but would have been false. And since Allah's report is a matter that is necessarily binding, it is inevitably the case that falling into the painful punishment is required. Muqatil said: His statement, exalted is He, ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us,﴾ refers to Allah's word to Iblis: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all together﴾ [Sad 38:85]. And His statement, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, we are going to taste [it],﴾ means: since it was necessary that the word of our Lord come into effect against us, it was necessary that we be those who taste this punishment.

The fifth: their statement, ﴿So we led you astray; indeed, we were ourselves astray.﴾ The meaning is that we only proceeded to lead you astray because we were ourselves characterized by misguidance. There is also another subtle point in this: as if they were saying, "If you believe that your misguidance is caused by our misleading you, then our misguidance, if it was caused by the misleading of another misguided person, would lead to an infinite regress (tasalsul), and that is impossible. Therefore we know that the occurrence of misguidance and guidance is not from us, but from another. And that other is the one He mentioned earlier, namely His statement: ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us.﴾"

When Allah, exalted is He, related the speech of the followers to the leaders and the speech of the leaders to the followers, He then said: ﴿So on that Day they will be sharing in the punishment.﴾ That is, the one who is followed and the follower, the one who is served and the servant, will share in falling into punishment, just as they were sharing in misguidance in this world. Then He said again: ﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals.﴾ By "the criminals" here He means the disbelievers, as evidence by His saying after this statement: ﴿Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they would be arrogant.﴾ The pronoun in His statement ﴿Indeed, they﴾ refers back to the preceding mention, which is His statement ﴿the criminals.﴾ This indicates that the unqualified term "criminal" (mujrim) is restricted in the Qur'an to the disbeliever. Then Allah, exalted is He, made clear that they fell into that punishment only because they were denying monotheism and prophethood. As for denying monotheism, it is His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they would be arrogant.﴾ That is, they would deny it, be zealous in upholding polytheism, and disdain to acknowledge monotheism.

As for denying prophethood, it is their statement: ﴿Are we to abandon our gods for a mad poet?﴾ They meant Muhammad. Then Allah, exalted is He, refuted them in that statement, saying: ﴿Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers.﴾ The explanation of this statement is that he brought the true religion, because it is established by reason that Allah, exalted is He, is free from any opposite, equal, or partner. So when Muhammad (ﷺ) came with establishing these meanings, his coming was with the true religion.

Ibn Kathir read: "a'yna la-tarikuw ālihatana" (أيْنا لَتارِكُوا آلِهَتَنا), with a hamza and a light, unstressed, non-prolonged ya after it. Nafi', in the transmission of Qalun, and Abu 'Amr, according to this interpretation, prolonged it. The rest read it with two hamzas without prolongation.

His statement, exalted is He, ﴿and confirmed the messengers,﴾ means: he confirmed them in their coming with monotheism and the negation of partners. This is an alert that affirming monotheism is the religion of all the prophets.

When Allah related their denial of monotheism and prophethood, He shifted the speech from the third person (absence) to the second person (presence), and said: ﴿Indeed, you are going to taste the painful punishment.﴾ It is as if it were said: how is it fitting for the Merciful, the Generous, who is exalted above benefit and harm, to punish His servants? He answered this with His statement: ﴿And you are being recompensed only for what you used to do.﴾ The meaning is that wisdom requires commanding what is good and obedience and forbidding what is ugly and disobedience. Commanding and forbidding do not achieve their purpose except through encouragement with reward and warning with punishment. When a report about this is given, it must be realized, to preserve speech from falsehood. For this reason they fell into punishment. Then He said: ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah.﴾ That is, but the sincere servants of Allah [are saved, and this is] an disjunct exception (istithna' munqati').

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, related that some of them would turn toward others, questioning one another, He explained the manner of that questioning. They said: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right.﴾ This is the statement of the followers to those who invited them to misguidance. Regarding the interpretation (tafsir, explanation) of "the right" (al-yamin) there are several aspects:

The first: the word "the right" here is a metaphor (isti'arah) for good things and felicities. The explanation of how this metaphor works is that the right side is superior to the left side, for several reasons:

One of them: all agree that the nobler of the two sides is the right.

The second: they do not undertake noble actions except with the right hand, such as shaking hands with the righteous, eating and drinking, whereas the opposite of these they do with the left hand.

The third: they used to seek omens of good luck, and they would consider the right side auspicious and call it "al-barih."

The fourth: the Prophet (ﷺ) loved to start with the right in everything.

The fifth: the Sharia ruled that the right side belongs to the recorder of good deeds and the left to the recorder of bad deeds.

The sixth: Allah, exalted is He, promised that the doer of good would be given his record in his right hand, and the doer of evil in his left hand. Thus it is established that the right side is superior to the left. Since this is so, it is inevitably the case that the word "right" is borrowed for good things, good deeds and acts of obedience. So His statement, ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right,﴾ means: you used to deceive us and give us the impression that your purpose in calling us to those religions was to support the truth and strengthen what is right.

The second aspect of interpretation: it is said, "So-and-so is the right [hand] of so-and-so" when he holds a good position with him. So these disbelievers said to their leaders, who had misled them and made disbelief attractive to them: you used to deceive us and give us the impression that we held a position of the right with you, that is, a good position, so we trusted you and accepted from you.

The third aspect: the leaders of disbelief had sworn to these weak ones that what they were calling them to was the truth. So they trusted their oaths and held to their covenants which they had made with them. Thus the meaning of His statement, ﴿you used to come to us from the right,﴾ is: from the direction of the pledges and oaths which you had given us.

The fourth aspect: the word "the right" is borrowed from strength and dominance, because the right hand is characterized by force, and it is with it that seizing occurs. The meaning is: you used to come to us from strength and dominance, and you aimed at us through authority and superiority, until you compelled us toward error and reproached us for it.

Then Allah, exalted is He, related that the leaders replied to the followers in several ways:

The first: they said to them, ﴿Rather, you were not believers,﴾ meaning: you were never characterized by faith such that it could be said that we removed you from it.

The second: their statement, ﴿And we had no authority over you,﴾ meaning: we had no power over you to overpower and compel you.

The third: ﴿Rather, you were a rebellious people,﴾ that is, you were going astray and exceeding the bounds in disobedience to Allah.

The fourth: their statement, ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us: indeed, we are going to taste [the punishment].﴾

Regarding the interpretation (tafsir, explanation) of "the right" (al-yamin) there are several aspects:

The first: the word "the right" here is a metaphor (isti'arah) for good things and felicities. The explanation of how this metaphor works is that the right side is superior to the left side, for several reasons:

One of them: all agree that the nobler of the two sides is the right.

The second: they do not undertake noble actions except with the right hand, such as shaking hands with the righteous, eating and drinking, whereas the opposite of these they do with the left hand.

The third: they used to seek omens of good luck, and they would consider the right side auspicious and call it "al-barih."

The fourth: the Prophet (ﷺ) loved to start with the right in everything.

The fifth: the Sharia ruled that the right side belongs to the recorder of good deeds and the left to the recorder of bad deeds.

The sixth: Allah, exalted is He, promised that the doer of good would be given his record in his right hand, and the doer of evil in his left hand. The fourth aspect: the word "the right" is borrowed from strength and dominance, because the right hand is characterized by force, and it is with it that seizing occurs. The meaning is: you used to come to us from strength and dominance, and you aimed at us through authority and superiority, until you compelled us toward error and reproached us for it.

The fifth: the Sharia ruled that the right side belongs to the recorder of good deeds and the left to the recorder of bad deeds.

Regarding the interpretation (tafsir, explanation) of "the right" (al-yamin) there are several aspects:

The first: the word "the right" here is a metaphor (isti'arah) for good things and felicities. The explanation of how this metaphor works is that the right side is superior to the left side, for several reasons:

One of them: all agree that the nobler of the two sides is the right.

The second: they do not undertake noble actions except with the right hand, such as shaking hands with the righteous, eating and drinking, whereas the opposite of these they do with the left hand.

The third: they used to seek omens of good luck, and they would consider the right side auspicious and call it "al-barih."

The fourth: the Prophet (ﷺ) loved to start with the right in everything.

The fifth: the Sharia ruled that the right side belongs to the recorder of good deeds and the left to the recorder of bad deeds.

The sixth: Allah, exalted is He, promised that the doer of good would be given his record in his right hand, and the doer of evil in his left hand. The meaning is: you used to come to us from strength and dominance, and you aimed at us through authority and superiority, until you compelled us toward error and reproached us for it.

The fourth: their statement, ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us: indeed, we are going to taste [the punishment].﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, related that some of them would turn toward others, questioning one another, He explained the manner of that questioning. They said: ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right.﴾ This is the statement of the followers to those who invited them to misguidance. Regarding the interpretation (tafsir, explanation) of "the right" (al-yamin) there are several aspects:

The first: the word "the right" here is a metaphor (isti'arah) for good things and felicities. The explanation of how this metaphor works is that the right side is superior to the left side, for several reasons:

One of them: all agree that the nobler of the two sides is the right.

The second: they do not undertake noble actions except with the right hand, such as shaking hands with the righteous, eating and drinking, whereas the opposite of these they do with the left hand.

The third: they used to seek omens of good luck, and they would consider the right side auspicious and call it "al-barih."

The fourth: the Prophet (ﷺ) loved to start with the right in everything.

The fifth: the Sharia ruled that the right side belongs to the recorder of good deeds and the left to the recorder of bad deeds.

The sixth: Allah, exalted is He, promised that the doer of good would be given his record in his right hand, and the doer of evil in his left hand. Thus it is established that the right side is superior to the left. Since this is so, it is inevitably the case that the word "right" is borrowed for good things, good deeds and acts of obedience. So His statement, ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right,﴾ means: you used to deceive us and give us the impression that your purpose in calling us to those religions was to support the truth and strengthen what is right.

The second aspect of interpretation: it is said, "So-and-so is the right [hand] of so-and-so" when he holds a good position with him. So these disbelievers said to their leaders, who had misled them and made disbelief attractive to them: you used to deceive us and give us the impression that we held a position of the right with you, that is, a good position, so we trusted you and accepted from you.

The third aspect: the leaders of disbelief had sworn to these weak ones that what they were calling them to was the truth. So they trusted their oaths and held to their covenants which they had made with them. Thus the meaning of His statement, ﴿you used to come to us from the right,﴾ is: from the direction of the pledges and oaths which you had given us.

The fourth aspect: the word "the right" is borrowed from strength and dominance, because the right hand is characterized by force, and it is with it that seizing occurs. The meaning is: you used to come to us from strength and dominance, and you aimed at us through authority and superiority, until you compelled us toward error and reproached us for it.

Then Allah, exalted is He, related that the leaders replied to the followers in several ways:

The first: they said to them, ﴿Rather, you were not believers,﴾ meaning: you were never characterized by faith such that it could be said that we removed you from it.

The second: their statement, ﴿And we had no authority over you,﴾ meaning: we had no power over you to overpower and compel you.

The third: ﴿Rather, you were a rebellious people,﴾ that is, you were going astray and exceeding the bounds in disobedience to Allah.

The fourth: their statement, ﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us: indeed, we are going to taste [the punishment].﴾

﴿They will be served with a cup from a flowing spring, white, delicious to those who drink,﴾ ﴿neither harmful to the mind nor will they be intoxicated by it,﴾ ﴿and with them will be maidens restraining their gaze, with beautiful eyes,﴾ ﴿as if they were hidden eggs.﴾ ﴿So they will turn to one another, questioning each other.﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, had described the condition of those who were arrogant about accepting tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), and who persisted in denying prophethood (nubuwwah), He followed it with mention of the condition of the sincere (al-mukhlasin) in the manner of their reward. In this there are several issues.

The first issue: we have mentioned two readings concerning the vowelling of the lam in ﴿al-mukhlasin﴾, with a fatha and with a kasra. The fatha means that Allah, exalted is He, made them sincere through His kindness and chose them through His favour. The kasra means that they made their obedience sincere to Allah, exalted is He.

The second issue: know that Allah, exalted is He, described their provision as being "known," but He did not specify which of its attributes is the known one, so the opinions differed. It was said: its meaning is that this provision is known in its time, namely the measure of morning and evening, even if there is neither morning nor evening there. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾ [Maryam: 62]. It was said: its meaning is that this provision is known in its quality, because it is specially distinguished by characteristics that Allah created in it of good taste, fragrance, delight, and beauty of appearance. It was said: its meaning is that they are certain of its permanence, unlike the provision of this world, which is not known when it will come nor when it will end. It was said: its meaning is the amount they deserve by their deeds of the reward of Allah and His honour upon them. Allah, exalted is He, has made clear that He gives them other than that by way of bounty. Then, when Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that they have a provision, He made clear what that provision is, saying: ﴿fruits﴾. Concerning this there are two statements.

The first: fruit (al-fakihah) is a term for what is eaten for the sake of enjoyment, not for the sake of need. The provisions of the people of Paradise are all fruits, because they are free from the need to preserve health by staple foods, for they are solid bodies created for eternity. So everything they eat is by way of enjoyment.

The second: the purpose of mentioning fruit is to draw attention from the lower to the higher. That is, since fruit is always present, condiments (al-idam) are more deserving of being present. The first statement is closer to verification. Know that when Allah, exalted is He, mentioned eating, He made clear that this eating occurs together with honour and esteem, so He said: ﴿and they will be honoured﴾, because eating devoid of esteem befits beasts.

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned their food, He described their dwellings, saying: ﴿in Gardens of Bliss, on couches facing one another.﴾ Its meaning is that there is no hardship for them in meeting for companionship and conversation. In some reports it is said that when they wished to draw near, the couch moved beneath them. It is not possible for them to be facing one another except with the presence of mutual regard and inner feelings, and they will not be so except with spaciousness and expanse. It is also not possible for one of them to hear the speech of another and see him from a distance except by Allah strengthening their sight, their hearing, and their voices.

When Allah explained the attribute of eating and dwelling, He mentioned after it the attribute of drinking, saying: ﴿They will be served with a cup from a flowing spring.﴾ The cup (ka's) is said of the glass in which there is wine, and the wine itself is also called a cup. He said:

"I drank from a cup for pleasure, and another time I was treated with it."

And from al-Akhfash: every cup in the Qur'an is wine. His saying ﴿from a flowing spring﴾ means: from a flowing drink, or from a flowing river. Al-ma'in is derived from the eye of water, meaning it flows from the springs as water flows, and it was called ma'in for its manifestness. It is said: "the water flowed" (ʿaana al-ma'u) when it appeared flowing. This is what Tha'lab said. So it is a passive form (maf'ul) from the eye (al-ayn), like mabi' and makil. It was also said: it was called ma'in because it flows from the surface of the spring. It is also possible that it is fa'il from al-ma'in, which is water of strong flow, and from this comes "he advanced in the journey" when he pressed on in it. His saying ﴿white﴾ is an attribute of the wine. Al-Akhfash said: the wine of Paradise is whiter than milk. His saying ﴿delicious﴾ has several meanings:

First: it has been described as delight, as if it were the very essence and substance of delight, just as one says "so-and-so is generosity and nobility" when they wish to intensify the description of him with these two attributes.

Second: al-Zajjaj said: that is, possessing delight, so the noun has been omitted.

Third: al-Layth said: al-ladhdh and al-ladhidh run in the same course as descriptors, and one says "a drink that is ladhdh and ladhidh." Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿delicious to those who drink﴾, and He said: ﴿of wine delicious﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. For this reason sleep is called ladhdh because of the pleasure one takes in it. According to this, ﴿ladhdhah﴾ means ladhidhah. The closest of these meanings is the first.

* * *

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿to those who drink﴾, ﴿neither harmful to the mind﴾. Concerning this there are some discussions.

The first discussion: al-Farra' said: the Arabs say, "there is no ghilah (seduction), no ghā'ilah (destruction), and no ghawl (harm) in it," all alike. Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-ghawl is that it seizes their minds. He recited the verse of Mut'i' ibn Iyas:

"The cup kept seizing them, and it takes away the first and the foremost."

Al-Layth said: al-ghawl is headache, and the meaning is that there is no headache in it as there is in the wine of this world. Al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: its real meaning is destruction. It is said: "he ghala him ghawlan," meaning he destroyed him. Al-ghawl and al-ghā'il are that which destroys. Then headache was called ghawl because it leads to destruction.

* * *

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿nor will they be intoxicated by it.﴾ It is read with a kasra on the zay. Al-Farra' said: whoever reads with a kasra on the zay has two meanings. It is said: "anzafa al-rajul" when his wine runs out, and "anzafa" when his mind is gone from intoxication. Whoever reads with a fatha on the zay, its meaning is: their minds will not go, that is, they will not become intoxicated. It is said: "nazafa al-rajul," so he is manzuf and nazif. The meaning is that there is never in it any kind of corruption that occurs in drinking wine, such as headache, hangover, or raving, and neither will they become drunk. He specified it by mention because it is the greatest of the corruptions in drinking wine. When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the attribute of their drink, He mentioned after it the attribute of their spouses in three respects:

The first: His saying ﴿and with them will be maidens restraining their gaze﴾. The meaning of qasr in language is restraint, and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Houris cloistered in pavilions﴾ [al-Rahman: 72]. The meaning is that they restrain their gaze and do not look at anyone other than their husbands.

The second attribute: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿ʿin﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: large-eyed and beautiful, and its singular is ʿaynaʾ.

The third attribute: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿as if they were hidden eggs.﴾ Al-maknun in language means concealed. It is said: "kanantu al-shay'a" and "akmantuhu," meaning I concealed the thing. The meaning of this comparison is that the outer surface of an egg is whiteness mixed with a little yellowness. [Page 120]

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, had described the condition of those who were arrogant about accepting tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), and who persisted in denying prophethood (nubuwwah), He followed it with mention of the condition of the sincere (al-mukhlasin) in the manner of their reward. In this there are several issues.

The first issue: we have mentioned two readings concerning the vowelling of the lam in ﴿al-mukhlasin﴾, with a fatha and with a kasra. The fatha means that Allah, exalted is He, made them sincere through His kindness and chose them through His favour. The kasra means that they made their obedience sincere to Allah, exalted is He.

The second issue: know that Allah, exalted is He, described their provision as being "known," but He did not specify which of its attributes is the known one, so the opinions differed. It was said: its meaning is that this provision is known in its time, namely the measure of morning and evening, even if there is neither morning nor evening there. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening﴾ [Maryam: 62]. It was said: its meaning is that this provision is known in its quality, because it is specially distinguished by characteristics that Allah created in it of good taste, fragrance, delight, and beauty of appearance. It was said: its meaning is that they are certain of its permanence, unlike the provision of this world, which is not known when it will come nor when it will end. It was said: its meaning is the amount they deserve by their deeds of the reward of Allah and His honour upon them. Allah, exalted is He, has made clear that He gives them other than that by way of bounty. Then, when Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that they have a provision, He made clear what that provision is, saying: ﴿fruits﴾. Concerning this there are two statements.

The first: fruit (al-fakihah) is a term for what is eaten for the sake of enjoyment, not for the sake of need. The provisions of the people of Paradise are all fruits, because they are free from the need to preserve health by staple foods, for they are solid bodies created for eternity. So everything they eat is by way of enjoyment.

The second: the purpose of mentioning fruit is to draw attention from the lower to the higher. That is, since fruit is always present, condiments (al-idam) are more deserving of being present. The first statement is closer to verification. Know that when Allah, exalted is He, mentioned eating, He made clear that this eating occurs together with honour and esteem, so He said: ﴿and they will be honoured﴾, because eating devoid of esteem befits beasts.

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned their food, He described their dwellings, saying: ﴿in Gardens of Bliss, on couches facing one another.﴾ Its meaning is that there is no hardship for them in meeting for companionship and conversation. In some reports it is said that when they wished to draw near, the couch moved beneath them. It is not possible for them to be facing one another except with the presence of mutual regard and inner feelings, and they will not be so except with spaciousness and expanse. It is also not possible for one of them to hear the speech of another and see him from a distance except by Allah strengthening their sight, their hearing, and their voices.

When Allah explained the attribute of eating and dwelling, He mentioned after it the attribute of drinking, saying: ﴿They will be served with a cup from a flowing spring.﴾ The cup (ka's) is said of the glass in which there is wine, and the wine itself is also called a cup. He said:

"I drank from a cup for pleasure, and another time I was treated with it."

And from al-Akhfash: every cup in the Qur'an is wine. His saying ﴿from a flowing spring﴾ means: from a flowing drink, or from a flowing river. Al-ma'in is derived from the eye of water, meaning it flows from the springs as water flows, and it was called ma'in for its manifestness. It is said: "the water flowed" (ʿaana al-ma'u) when it appeared flowing. This is what Tha'lab said. So it is a passive form (maf'ul) from the eye (al-ayn), like mabi' and makil. It was also said: it was called ma'in because it flows from the surface of the spring. It is also possible that it is fa'il from al-ma'in, which is water of strong flow, and from this comes "he advanced in the journey" when he pressed on in it. His saying ﴿white﴾ is an attribute of the wine. Al-Akhfash said: the wine of Paradise is whiter than milk. His saying ﴿delicious﴾ has several meanings:

First: it has been described as delight, as if it were the very essence and substance of delight, just as one says "so-and-so is generosity and nobility" when they wish to intensify the description of him with these two attributes.

Second: al-Zajjaj said: that is, possessing delight, so the noun has been omitted.

Third: al-Layth said: al-ladhdh and al-ladhidh run in the same course as descriptors, and one says "a drink that is ladhdh and ladhidh." Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿delicious to those who drink﴾, and He said: ﴿of wine delicious﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. For this reason sleep is called ladhdh because of the pleasure one takes in it. According to this, ﴿ladhdhah﴾ means ladhidhah. The closest of these meanings is the first.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 37, verse 51–61:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Said one of them, "Indeed, I had a companion"﴾ ﴿who used to say, "Are you really among those who believe?"﴾ ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be recompensed?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Would you like to look down?"﴾ ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Hellfire.﴾ ﴿He said, "By Allah, you were about to ruin me!﴾ ﴿Had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forward [to punishment]."﴾ ﴿"Then are we not to die﴾ ﴿except for our first death, and we will not be punished?"﴾ ﴿Indeed, this is the great triumph."﴾ ﴿For the likes of this let the workers work.﴾ Concerning the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: Know that He, exalted is He, as He mentioned concerning the people of Paradise that they ask one another when they gather to drink the wine of Paradise, since conversing among intelligent people with one another while drinking is among pleasurable things, and recalling deliverance when the causes of destruction have gathered is among pleasurable things, He, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse that when the people of Paradise gather to drink and begin conversing and questioning, among those words is that they remember that in the world there had occurred to them what would have made them fall into the punishment of Allah, and then they were delivered from it and won eternal happiness. The purpose of mentioning these things is that the joy and delight of the people of Paradise be completed.

As for His saying: ﴿Said one of them, "Indeed, I had a companion"﴾, meaning: one speaker among the people of Paradise said, "Indeed, I had a companion in the world" ﴿who used to say, "Are you really among those who believe?"﴾, meaning he used to rebuke me for affirming the resurrection and the Last Day, and he would say in amazement: ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be recompensed?"﴾, meaning, will we be called to account and requited? The meaning is that this companion used to say these words in denial. Then that man, who is among the people of Paradise, says to his companions, inviting them to complete joy by looking down into the Fire to witness that companion and to address him: ﴿"Would you like to look down?"﴾ ﴿So he looked﴾. The closer view is that he made an effort to look, along with them, because if he were looking down without effort there would be no need for his looking; therefore some have said that he went to one of the edges of Paradise and looked down from there into the Fire. ﴿And saw him in the midst of the Hellfire﴾, meaning: in the middle of the Blazing Fire. He said to him, rebuking him: ﴿"By Allah, you were about to ruin me!"﴾, meaning: you would have destroyed me by your calling me to deny the resurrection and the Last Day. ﴿"Had it not been for the favor of my Lord"﴾ by guiding me to the truth and protecting me from falsehood ﴿"I would have been among those brought forward [to punishment]"﴾ in the Fire like you. When he had completed that speech with the man who had been his companion in the world, and who is now among the people of the Fire, he returned to addressing his companions who are among the people of Paradise, and said: ﴿"Then are we not to die"﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

The first: the people of Paradise do not know, when they first enter Paradise, that they will not die; then when Death is brought in the form of a white-speckled ram and is slaughtered, at that point they know that they will not die. So perhaps this statement occurred before the slaughter of Death.

The second: one whose good and happiness are complete, when his wonder at them becomes great, may say, "Will this endure for me? Will this remain for me?" even though he is certain of its permanence. Then, when they finish these discussions, they say: ﴿"Indeed, this is the great triumph."﴾

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿"For the likes of this let the workers work."﴾ it is said that it is part of their speech, and it is said that it is the beginning of a speech from Allah, exalted is He, meaning: to seek the likes of these happinesses, the workers must work.

The second issue: Some have said: what is meant by this speaker and his companion is what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in Surah al-Kahf in His saying: ﴿"And strike for them an example: two men"﴾ [al-Kahf: 32] to the end of the verses. It is related that two men were partners, and they acquired eight thousand dinars. One of them said to the other, "I will divide it with you," and he divided it with him. He bought a house for a thousand dinars and showed it to his companion, and said, "How do you find its beauty?" He said, "How beautiful it is!" He went out and said, "O Allah, indeed my companion here has bought this house for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a house from the houses of Paradise," so he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then his companion married a beautiful woman for a thousand dinars, and this one gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then his companion bought gardens for two thousand dinars, and this one gave two thousand dinars in charity. Then Allah gave him in Paradise what he asked for. At this point he said: ﴿"Indeed, I had a companion"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿"So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Hellfire."﴾

The third issue: As for His saying: ﴿"Are you really among those who believe?"﴾ ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be recompensed?"﴾, the readers differed concerning these three interrogatives. Nafi' read the first and second with an interrogative hamzah not extended, and the third with a kasra on the alif without interrogation; al-Kisa'i agreed with him, except that he reads the third as interrogative with two hamzahs. Ibn 'Amir read the first and third with interrogation using two hamzahs, and the second with a kasra on the alif without interrogation. The rest read all of them with interrogation. Then they differed: Ibn Kathir uses a single hamzah, not lengthened, followed by a light, sukun yā'; Abu 'Amr uses a lengthened one; 'Asim and Hamzah use two hamzahs.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿"Indeed, I had a companion"﴾, ﴿"You were about to ruin me"﴾, Nafi', through the transmission of Warsh, reads *latturdini* with the yā' pronounced in continuation, while the rest omit it.

The fourth issue: Our companions argued that guidance and misguidance are from Allah, exalted is He, by His saying: ﴿"Had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forward"﴾. They said: the opponent's position is that everything of the forms of bounty which Allah, exalted is He, does for the believer, He also does for the disbeliever. If that bounty is shared, it is impossible for it to be the cause of the believer's guidance and of his deliverance from disbelief and perdition. Therefore that specific favor must be something additional beyond those shared bounties, and this is none other than the strengthening of the motive toward faith and the completion of what turns one away from disbelief.

The fifth issue: Those who deny the punishment of the grave argued with the words of the man from the people of Paradise: ﴿"Then are we not to die﴾ ﴿except for our first death"﴾. This indicates that a person dies only once; and if life were attained in the grave, death would have occurred twice. The answer: His saying ﴿"except for our first death"﴾ refers to everything that happened in the world, and Allah knows best.

He said to him, rebuking him: ﴿"By Allah, you were about to ruin me!"﴾, meaning: you would have destroyed me by your calling me to deny the resurrection and the Last Day. ﴿"Had it not been for the favor of my Lord"﴾ by guiding me to the truth and protecting me from falsehood ﴿"I would have been among those brought forward [to punishment]"﴾ in the Fire like you. When he had completed that speech with the man who had been his companion in the world, and who is now among the people of the Fire, he returned to addressing his companions who are among the people of Paradise, and said: ﴿"Then are we not to die"﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

The first: the people of Paradise do not know, when they first enter Paradise, that they will not die; then when Death is brought in the form of a white-speckled ram and is slaughtered, at that point they know that they will not die. So perhaps this statement occurred before the slaughter of Death.

The second: one whose good and happiness are complete, when his wonder at them becomes great, may say, "Will this endure for me? Will this remain for me?" even though he is certain of its permanence. Then, when they finish these discussions, they say: ﴿"Indeed, this is the great triumph."﴾

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿"For the likes of this let the workers work."﴾ it is said that it is part of their speech, and it is said that it is the beginning of a speech from Allah, exalted is He, meaning: to seek the likes of these happinesses, the workers must work.

The second issue: Some have said: what is meant by this speaker and his companion is what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in Surah al-Kahf in His saying: ﴿"And strike for them an example: two men"﴾ [al-Kahf: 32] to the end of the verses. It is related that two men were partners, and they acquired eight thousand dinars. One of them said to the other, "I will divide it with you," and he divided it with him. He bought a house for a thousand dinars and showed it to his companion, and said, "How do you find its beauty?" He said, "How beautiful it is!" He went out and said, "O Allah, indeed my companion here has bought this house for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a house from the houses of Paradise," so he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then his companion married a beautiful woman for a thousand dinars, and this one gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then his companion bought gardens for two thousand dinars, and this one gave two thousand dinars in charity. Then Allah gave him in Paradise what he asked for. At this point he said: ﴿"Indeed, I had a companion"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿"So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Hellfire."﴾

The third issue: As for His saying: ﴿"Are you really among those who believe?"﴾ ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be recompensed?"﴾, the readers differed concerning these three interrogatives. Nafi' read the first and second with an interrogative hamzah not extended, and the third with a kasra on the alif without interrogation; al-Kisa'i agreed with him, except that he reads the third as interrogative with two hamzahs. Ibn 'Amir read the first and third with interrogation using two hamzahs, and the second with a kasra on the alif without interrogation. The rest read all of them with interrogation. Then they differed: Ibn Kathir uses a single hamzah, not lengthened, followed by a light, sukun yā'; Abu 'Amr uses a lengthened one; 'Asim and Hamzah use two hamzahs.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿"Indeed, I had a companion"﴾, ﴿"You were about to ruin me"﴾, Nafi', through the transmission of Warsh, reads *latturdini* with the yā' pronounced in continuation, while the rest omit it.

The fourth issue: Our companions argued that guidance and misguidance are from Allah, exalted is He, by His saying: ﴿"Had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forward"﴾. They said: the opponent's position is that everything of the forms of bounty which Allah, exalted is He, does for the believer, He also does for the disbeliever. If that bounty is shared, it is impossible for it to be the cause of the believer's guidance and of his deliverance from disbelief and perdition. Therefore that specific favor must be something additional beyond those shared bounties, and this is none other than the strengthening of the motive toward faith and the completion of what turns one away from disbelief.

The fifth issue: Those who deny the punishment of the grave argued with the words of the man from the people of Paradise: ﴿"Then are we not to die﴾ ﴿except for our first death"﴾. This indicates that a person dies only once; and if life were attained in the grave, death would have occurred twice. The answer: His saying ﴿"except for our first death"﴾ refers to everything that happened in the world, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 37, verse 62–75:

Page 123

﴿So look, how was the end of those who were warned?﴾ ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum?﴾ ﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs forth from the root of Hell-fire.﴾ ﴿Its fruit-spathes are as if they were the heads of devils.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies from it.﴾ ﴿Then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of boiling water.﴾ ﴿Then indeed their return is to Hell-fire.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray.﴾ ﴿So they were hastening in their footsteps.﴾ ﴿And certainly did most of the earlier people go astray before them.﴾ ﴿And certainly We sent among them warners.﴾ ﴿So look, how was the end of those who were warned?﴾ ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah.﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, said, after mentioning the people of Paradise and its description, ﴿For the likes of this let the workers work﴾, He followed it with His saying: ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum?﴾ So He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to present this to the disbelievers of his people, so that it would be a deterrent for them from disbelief. Just as He had earlier described the food and drink of the people of Paradise, He also describes in this verse the food and drink of the people of the Fire.

As for His saying: ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum?﴾, the meaning is that the provision known and mentioned for the people of Paradise ﴿is that better as a welcome﴾, meaning better in what it yields, ﴿or the tree of al-Zaqqum?﴾. The root of nuzul (welcome, provision) is abundant surplus of food; it is said: "a food abundant in nuzul" (kathir al-nuzul). It was then borrowed for what results from a thing. It is also said: "The commander sent to so-and-so a nuzul," meaning the thing that suits the state of the one who lodges by means of it. Once you know this, we say: the outcome of the known provision for the people of Paradise is pleasure and joy, and the outcome of the tree of al-Zaqqum is pain and grief. It is known that there is no comparison between the two in terms of goodness, except that this statement came either as mockery of them, or because the believers, when they chose what led them to the noble provision, and the disbelievers chose what led them to the painful punishment, it was said to them as a reproach for their poor choice.

As for "al-Zaqqum", al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The exegetes did not mention an explanation of al-Zaqqum except al-Kalbi, for he narrated that when this verse was revealed, Ibn al-Za'bari said: "May Allah multiply zaqqum in your houses, for the people of Yemen call dates and butter by the name zaqqum." Then Abu Jahl said to his slave-girl: "Zaqqimina!" So she brought him butter and dates, and he said: "Eat your fill (tazaqqamu)." Then al-Wahidi said: It is known that Allah, exalted is He, did not intend by al-Zaqqum here butter and dates. Ibn Duraid said: al-Zaqqum has no derivation from tazaqqum, which is excessive eating of a thing to the point that it becomes disliked; it is said: "So-and-so spent the night tazaqqamu." The apparent wording of the Qur'an indicates that it is a tree whose food is disgusting, whose smell is foul, and whose roughness is severe, described with attributes such that whoever partakes of it is greatly harmed by partaking of it. Then Allah, exalted is He, compels the people of the Fire to partake of some of its parts.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers.﴾ there are several views:

The first: it became a trial for the wrongdoers in that when the disbelievers heard this verse, they said: "How is it conceivable that a tree should grow in Hell, when the Fire burns trees?"

The answer to this is that the Creator of the Fire is able to prevent the Fire from burning the tree. Moreover, if it is permissible that there be guardians (zabaniyah) in the Fire while Allah prevents the Fire from burning them, why should the like not be permissible for this tree? Once you know this question, and the answer, the meaning of the zaqqum tree being a trial for the wrongdoers is that when they heard this verse, that doubt entered their hearts, and that doubt became a cause for their persistence in disbelief. This is what is meant by it being a trial for them.

The second interpretation is that the intended meaning is that this tree becomes a trial for them in the Fire; for when they are obligated to partake of it and it is hard for them, then it becomes a trial for them.

The third interpretation: that the intended meaning of trial (fitnah) is testing and examination, for this is a matter far removed from custom and habit, contrary to what is familiar and known. So when it reaches the hearing of a believer, he entrusts its knowledge to Allah; and when it reaches a heretic (zindiq), he uses it as a means to attack the Qur'an and prophethood.

Page 124

Then, when He mentioned this tree, He described it with attributes:

The first attribute: His saying, "Indeed, it is a tree that springs forth from the root of Hell-fire." It was said: its place of growth is at the bottom of Hell, and its branches rise up to its levels.

The second attribute: His saying: ﴿Its fruit-spathes are as if they were the heads of devils.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: talʿ (spathe/fruit-bud) is for the palm tree, so it was borrowed for what emerges from the zaqqum tree as its bearing, either as a lexical metaphor or a semantic metaphor. Ibn Qutaybah said: it was called "ṭalʿ" because it emerges (ṭulūʿ) every year, and for this reason it is said: "ṭalʿ al-nakhl" for the first thing that comes out of its fruit. As for the comparison of this ṭalʿ to the heads of devils, there is a question in it: it is said: "We have not seen the heads of devils, so how can anything be compared to them?" They answered this in several ways:

The first, which is the correct one: when people believed that angels possess perfect excellence in form and conduct, they believed that devils possess the utmost ugliness and deformity in form and conduct. Just as comparison to an angel is fine when intending to establish perfection and excellence, as in His saying: ﴿This is nothing but a noble angel﴾ [Yusuf: 31], so likewise it is fitting that comparison to the heads of devils be fine for ugliness and deformity of creation. The upshot is that this is a comparison not to the perceptible but to the imagined: as if it were said that the most hideous things in imagination and conception are the heads of devils, and this tree resembles them in the ugliness of its appearance and the deformity of its form. What confirms this is that when intelligent people see something highly disturbing, unusual in form, and hideous in creation, they say: "It is a devil"; and when they see something beautiful in form and conduct, they say: "It is an angel." Imru' al-Qays said:

"Will you kill me while the sharp sword is my bedfellow, and notched blades, blue, like the fangs of ghouls?"

The second view: the devils are snakes that have heads and crests, and they are among the most hideous of snakes, and by them the proverb of ugliness is struck. When the Arabs see an ugly sight they say: "It is like the devil of al-Hamataḥ," and al-Hamatah is a specific tree.

The third view: the heads of devils are a well-known plant with an ugly head. The first interpretation is the true answer.

Know that when He mentioned this tree and described its attributes, He made clear that the disbelievers are ﴿indeed eaters of it, and filling their bellies from it.﴾ Know that their undertaking of this eating has two possible aspects:

The first: they ate from it because of intense hunger. If it is said: "How do they eat it when it is extremely harsh, foul, and bitter in taste?" we say: one who falls into great harm may find relief in something that approximates that harm; so when Allah makes them feel intense hunger, they flee, to relieve that hunger, to partaking of this thing, even though it is of the quality you have mentioned.

The second aspect: it may be said that the zabaniyah compel them to eat from that tree, as a completion of their punishment.

Know that when they are satiated, their thirst then intensifies and they need drink. At this point Allah described their drink, saying: ﴿Then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of boiling water.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: al-shawb is a general name for anything mixed with something else, and al-hamim is hot water extremely intense in heat. The meaning is that when that intense thirst overcomes them, they are given to drink from that hamim, and then the zaqqum is mixed with the hamim—we seek refuge in Allah from both.

Know that Allah described their drink in the Qur'an with various things: among them that it is ghassaq; among them His saying: ﴿And they are given boiling water, so it cuts their intestines﴾ [Muhammad: 15]; and among them what He mentioned in this verse. If it is asked: what is the benefit of the particle "thumma" (then) in His saying: ﴿Then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of boiling water﴾? We say: it has two aspects:

The first: they fill their bellies with the tree of al-Zaqqum, which is hot and burns

Page 125

their bellies, so their thirst increases; then they are not given to drink except after a long period. The purpose is to complete the punishment.

The second: He mentioned the food with that foulness and repugnance, then described the drink with what is more repugnant than it; so the purpose of "thumma" is to show that the condition of the drink in repugnance is greater than the condition of the food. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then indeed their return is to Hell-fire.﴾ Muqatil said: that is, after eating the zaqqum and drinking the hamim. This indicates that when they were drinking the hamim they were not in Hell, and that is because the hamim comes from a place outside Hell; they are brought to the hamim for drinking as camels are brought to water, and then they are brought back to Hell. This is Muqatil's view, and he argued for its soundness by His saying: ﴿This is Hell which the criminals used to deny. They will circulate between it and scalding, boiling water﴾ [al-Rahman: 43–44], and this indicates the soundness of what we have mentioned. Then, when He described their punishment in their eating and drinking, He said: ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray.﴾ ﴿So they were hastening in their footsteps.﴾ Al-Farra' said: al-ihrā' is hastening; it is said: hara'a and ahra'a when one is urged on. The meaning is that they follow their fathers in haste, as if they were being driven to follow their fathers. The purpose of the verse is that He, exalted is He, gave as the reason for their deserving to fall into all those hardships the imitation of fathers in religion and the abandonment of following evidence; and had there been no verse in the Qur'an other than this one condemning blind imitation, it would have sufficed.

Then He, exalted is He, mentioned to His Messenger what would console him regarding their disbelief and denial, saying: ﴿And certainly did most of the earlier people go astray before them.﴾ ﴿And certainly We sent among them warners.﴾ Thus He, exalted is He, made clear that His sending of messengers had already preceded and that their denial had already passed; and it must be that he ﷺ has an example in them, so that he may be patient as they were patient, and persist in calling to Allah even if they rebel; for upon him there is only the delivering (of the message).

* * *

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So look, how was the end of those who were warned?﴾ Although this is outwardly an address to the Messenger ﷺ, its real purpose is an address to the disbelievers; for they have heard the reports of all the kinds of punishment that befell the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and others. If they did not know that, then there is at least a suspicion and fear fit to be a deterrent for them from their disbelief.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah﴾, there are two views:

One of them: it is an exception from His saying: ﴿And certainly did most of the earlier people go astray before them.﴾

The second: it is an exception from His saying: ﴿How was the end of those who were warned?﴾ for their end was the worst and most horrible of ends, except the end of the sincere servants of Allah, for it was accompanied by good and ease.
