He said: "No, but I was commanded to send a strong and trustworthy man, and you are such." Yunus said: "Among the Children of Israel there is one stronger than me, so why do you not send him?" The king insisted upon him, and Yunus became angry with him, and went out until he came to the Sea of Rum, and found a ship laden, and they carried him in it. When it entered the depths of the sea, it came close to sinking. The sailors said: "Among you there is a disobedient one, otherwise there would not have happened in the ship what we see without wind or apparent cause." He said: "O people, I am the disobedient one," and he wrapped himself in a cloak and threw himself down, and the fish swallowed him. Yunus grieved over that a great grief, and said: "O Lord, I used to shade myself beneath this tree from the sun and the wind, and suck from its fruit, and now it has fallen." It was said to him: "O Yunus, you grieve over a tree that was grown in an hour and uprooted in an hour, and you do not grieve over a hundred thousand or more whom you abandoned! Go to them." * * *

His saying ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾: it is said "alama" when one commits what deserves blame. So al-mulim is one who deserves blame, who has committed what is blameworthy.

* * *

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿while he was ailing﴾. It was said: what is meant is that his flesh had decayed and he became weak like a newborn child, like a fledgling plucked of its feathers, having no down. Mujahid said: "saqim" means "salib" (deprived of strength).

The merchants said: "We are more deserving of the sin than the prophet of Allah." Then they returned a second and third time, casting lots, and the lot of Yunus came out. He said: "O people, I am the disobedient one," and he wrapped himself in a cloak and threw himself down, and the fish swallowed him. Allah the Exalted revealed to the fish: "Do not break any bone of his, nor cut any joint of his." Then the fish brought him out to the Nile of Egypt, then to the Sea of Persia, then to the Sea of al-Bata'ih, then the Tigris, and it ascended with him and cast him on the land of Nasibin, in the open, and he was like a plucked fledgling, with no hair and no flesh. Allah caused to grow over him a gourd plant, and he would shade himself beneath it and eat from its fruit until he grew strong. Then the earth consumed it and it fell from its root. Yunus grieved over that a great grief, and said: "O Lord, I used to shade myself beneath this tree from the sun and the wind, and suck from its fruit, and now it has fallen." It was said to him: "O Yunus, you grieve over a tree that was grown in an hour and uprooted in an hour, and you do not grieve over a hundred thousand or more whom you abandoned! Go to them." And Allah knows best the reality of the event.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then the fish swallowed him, and he was blameworthy.﴾ It is said: "iltaqamahu" and "iltahamahu," both with the same meaning. His saying ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾: it is said "alama" when one commits what deserves blame. So al-mulim is one who deserves blame, who has committed what is blameworthy.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And had he not been of those who glorify Allah. He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ Regarding the explanation of his being among those who glorify, there are two views:

The first: what is meant is what Allah the Exalted related of him in another verse, that he was saying in those darknesses: ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾.

The second: that had he not been, before the fish swallowed him, among those who glorify, that is, those who pray, and had he not been constant in most times in the remembrance of Allah and His obedience, he would have remained in the belly of that fish, and its belly would have been a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: remember Allah in ease and He will remember you in hardship, for Yunus (peace be upon him) was a righteous servant, mindful of Allah the Exalted, so when he fell into the belly of the fish, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And had he not been of those who glorify Allah. He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ And Pharaoh was a tyrannical, forgetful servant, so when drowning overtook him he said: ﴿I believe that there is no god except He in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾ [Yunus: 90]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before﴾ [Yunus: 91].

They differed about how long he remained in the belly of the fish, and the wording of the Qur'an does not indicate it. al-Hasan said: he remained only a short while, and he was brought out from its belly after the time when it had swallowed him. From Muqatil ibn Hayyan: three days. From 'Ata': seven days. From al-Dahhak: twenty days. It was also said: a month. I do not know by what evidence they specified these measures.

From Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Yunus glorified Allah in the belly of the fish, and the angels heard his glorification, and they said: 'Our Lord, we hear a weak voice in a strange land.' He said: 'That is My servant Yunus, who disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the fish in the sea.' They said: 'The righteous servant from whom a righteous deed used to ascend to You every day and night?' He said: 'Yes.' So they interceded for him, and He commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the shore." That is His saying: ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾. And in this are several discussions:

The first: al-'ara' is the empty place. Abu 'Ubaydah said: it was called "al-'ara'" only because there is no tree in it and nothing covers it.

The second: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So We cast him onto the open shore﴾, attributing that casting to Himself, while the casting actually occurred through the action of the fish. This indicates that the act of the servant is created by Allah the Exalted.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿while he was ailing﴾. It was said: what is meant is that his flesh had decayed and he became weak like a newborn child, like a fledgling plucked of its feathers, having no down. Mujahid said: "saqim" means "salib" (deprived of strength).

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We caused to grow over him a gourd plant﴾. The apparent wording indicates that when the fish cast him onto the open shore, Allah the Exalted caused to grow over him a gourd plant, and that was a miracle for him. Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj said: every plant that does not stand on a stalk but spreads over the surface of the earth is "yaqtin," such as the squash, the colocynth, and the watermelon. Al-Zajjaj said: I think its derivation is from "qatana bi-al-makan" when he stayed in a place, and this plant's leaves all lie on the surface of the earth, so it was called yaqtin. Al-Farra' related that it was said in the presence of Ibn 'Abbas that it was the leaves of the pumpkin. He said: whoever makes the pumpkin among the trees a yaqtin... every leaf that spreads and provides cover is a yaqtin. Al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the verse implies two things that the exegetes did not mention:

One: that this yaqtin did not exist before, and Allah caused it to grow for his sake.

The other: that the yaqtin was trellised so that he would have shade, for if it had spread flat on the ground he would not have been able to shade himself beneath it.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾. In this there are several discussions:

The first: it is possible that what is meant is that We sent him before the fish swallowed him, and although this sending is mentioned after the swallowing, what is meant is precedence, and the conjunction "wa" means gathering. It is also possible that what is meant is the sending after the swallowing. From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he said: the mission of Yunus (peace be upon him) was after the fish cast him out. On this reckoning it is permissible that he was sent to a people other than the first people, and it is permissible that he was sent again to the first people with a law, and they believed in it.

The second discussion: the apparent wording of His saying ﴿or more﴾ implies doubt, and that is impossible for Allah the Exalted. Its parallels are His saying: ﴿as an excuse or a warning﴾ [al-Mursalat: 6], His saying: ﴿so that he may remember or fear﴾ [Ta-Ha: 44], His saying: ﴿so that they may fear Him or He may bring about for them a reminder﴾ [Ta-Ha: 113], His saying: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye or even nearer﴾ [al-Nahl: 77], and His saying: ﴿And he was two bow-lengths away or nearer﴾ [al-Najm: 9]. They answered this in many ways, and the most correct of them is one way: that the meaning is "or they exceed in your estimation," in the sense that when the observer sees them he says: these are a hundred thousand or more beyond the hundred. This is the answer for everything resembling this.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So they believed, and We let them enjoy [their lives] for a time.﴾ The meaning is that when those peoples believed, God removed the fear from them, secured them from the punishment, and God let them enjoy [worldly life] until a time, that is, until the appointed term that God set as the lifespan of each one of them.

**Page 146**

*His saying, may He be exalted:* ﴿So ask them: "Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?" Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?¹ Behold, it is from their own lie that they say, "Allah has begotten," and indeed they are liars. Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Will you not then take heed? Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your Book, if you are truthful. And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship; but the jinn know well that they will surely be brought forth. Glory be to Allah above what they describe, except for the sincere servants of Allah.﴾ And in this passage are several issues:

**The first issue:** Know that when Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned the stories of the Prophets, peace be upon them, He returned to explain the doctrines of the polytheists, and to show how ugly and feeble they are. Among their false statements is that they attributed offspring to Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, and then claimed that these offspring are of the female kind, not the male. So He said: ﴿So ask them: "Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?"﴾ This is connected to His words at the beginning of the surah: ﴿So ask them: are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?﴾ [al-Saffat: 11]. This is because Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to ask the Quraysh first about the basis of their denial of resurrection. Then the discourse continued, each part linked to the next, until He commanded him to ask them why they attributed daughters to Allah while attributing sons to themselves. Al-Wahidi reported from the commentators that they said: the Quraysh and the tribes of the Arabs, Juhayna, Banu Salama, Khuza'a and Banu Malih, said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Know that this statement contains two matters:

The first: the attribution of daughters to Allah, and this is false, because the Arabs used to disdain having daughters, and how could that which a created being disdains be attributed to the Creator?

The second: the claim that the angels are female, and this too is false. The ways of knowledge are either sense perception, or report, or reasoning. As for sense perception, it is absent here, because they did not witness the manner in which Allah created the angels, and this is what is meant by His words: ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾ As for report, it is also absent, because a report yields knowledge only when its truthfulness is known with certainty, and those who report this ruling are liars and deceivers; there is no proof or indication of their truthfulness. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿Behold, it is from their own lie that they say, "Allah has begotten," and indeed they are liars.﴾ As for reasoning, it too is absent, and its explanation is in two ways:

The first: the proof of reason requires the corruption of this doctrine, because Allah is the most perfect of beings, and it does not befit the Most Perfect to choose the most base. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ That is, attributing the more excellent to the more excellent is closer to reason than attributing the baser to the more excellent. So if the judgment of reason is to be considered in this matter, your saying is false.

The second way: we set aside arguing against the corruption of their doctrine, and instead demand that they produce the proof that establishes the soundness of their doctrine. If they do not find such proof, its opposite shows that nothing exists that proves the soundness of their claim. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your Book, if you are truthful.﴾ Thus, by what we have mentioned, it is established that the view they adopted is not supported by sense perception, report, or reasoning, so resorting to it is certainly false. Know that when He demanded of them what would prove the soundness of their doctrine, this indicates that imitation (taqlid) is false, and that religion is not sound except by proof.

**The second issue:** His words: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾ The reading of the majority is with a fatha on the hamza and with the hamza being a cut (qat') from ﴿aṣṭafā﴾, and then the alif of connection (alif al-wasl) is dropped. It is an interrogative of rebuke and reproach, like His words: ﴿Or has He taken daughters out of what He creates?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 16], and His words: ﴿Or has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ [al-Tur: 39], and His words: ﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him?﴾ [al-Najm: 21]. Just as all these places are interrogative, so too is this verse. Nafi' in some transmissions read: "la-kadhibūn, aṣṭafā" connected without interrogation. When he began, he would put a kasra on the hamza, in the manner of a statement, and the implied sense is "He chose daughters," according to their claim, like His words: ﴿Taste it, indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [al-Dukhan: 49], "according to his claim and belief."

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾, and they differed concerning what is meant by "the jinn," in several ways:

The first: Muqatil said: they established a kinship between Allah, exalted is He, and the angels, when they claimed that they are the daughters of Allah. According to this view, "the jinn" are the angels. They were called jinn because they are hidden from sight, or because they are the guardians of Paradise (al-Janna). I say that this view is problematic in my opinion, because He, exalted is He, refuted their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah, then joined to it His words: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship,﴾ and conjunction requires that the conjoined be different from what it is conjoined to, so this verse must mean something other than what preceded it.

The second: Mujahid said: the disbelievers of the Quraysh said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said to them: "Then who are their mothers?" They said: "The chieftains of the jinn." This too, in my view, is far-fetched, because marriage is not called kinship (nasab).

The third: We have narrated, in the interpretation of His words: ﴿And they have made for Allah partners, the jinn﴾ [al-An'am: 100], that a group of zanadiqa (heretics) said: "Allah and Iblis are brothers: Allah is the Good, the Generous, and Iblis is the evil, base brother." So His words: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾ mean this doctrine. In my view, this is the closest of the opinions, and it is the doctrine of the Magians (majus) who hold to Yazdan and Ahriman.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But the jinn know well that they will surely be brought forth﴾, meaning: the jinn know well that those who spoke this saying will be brought forth into the Fire and punished. It has also been said that the meaning is: the jinn know well that they will surely be brought forth to punishment. According to the first view, the pronoun refers to the speakers of this saying; according to the second view, it refers to the jinn themselves. Then He, exalted is He, declared Himself free of what they lied about, saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe, except for the sincere servants of Allah.﴾ Concerning this exception there are several views:

It has been said: it is an exception from "those brought forth," meaning that they are saved. It has been said: it is an exception from His words: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship.﴾ It has also been said: it is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati') from "those brought forth," and its meaning is: "But the sincere ones are free from describing Him with that." The word "mukhlis" with a kasra on the lam means one who makes his worship and belief sincere for Allah, and with a fatha on the lam means one whom Allah has purified by His kindness. And Allah knows best.

The first: the attribution of daughters to Allah, and this is false, because the Arabs used to disdain having daughters, and how could that which a created being disdains be attributed to the Creator?

This is what is meant by His words: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ That is, attributing the more excellent to the more excellent is closer to reason than attributing the baser to the more excellent. If they do not find such proof, its opposite shows that nothing exists that proves the soundness of their claim. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿Or do you have a clear authority? So bring your Book, if you are truthful.﴾ Thus, by what we have mentioned, it is established that the view they adopted is not supported by sense perception, report, or reasoning, so resorting to it is certainly false. **Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 37, verses 164–172**

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾ ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him﴾ ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾ ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾ ﴿And indeed, we are those who stand in ranks﴾ ﴿And indeed, we are those who glorify [Him]﴾ ﴿And indeed, they were saying﴾ ﴿"If only we had a reminder from the former peoples﴾ ﴿we would surely be sincere servants of God"﴾ ﴿But they disbelieved in it, so they will soon know.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Know that when God, exalted is He, mentioned the proofs against the corrupt doctrine of the disbelievers, He followed it with something that alerts to the fact that these disbelievers have no power to lead anyone astray unless God's judgment concerning him has already preceded, [determining] his punishment and his falling into the Fire. The author of *al-Kashshaf* (Zamakhshari's commentary) mentioned two opinions concerning God's words ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾ ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him﴾:

The first: the pronoun in ﴿against Him﴾ refers to God, the Mighty and Majestic. Its meaning is: "So indeed you and your objects of worship, you all together cannot lead astray against God anyone except the companions of the Fire, those whose being among the people of the Fire was already decreed in God's knowledge." If it is asked, "How can they lead them astray against God?" We say: they lead them astray against Him by their misguidance of them, from your saying "Fulan seduced Fulan against Fulan's wife" (fatana Fulan 'ala Fulan imra'atahu), just as you say "he corrupted her against him" (af sadaha 'alayhi).

The second possibility: the *waw* in His words ﴿and what you worship﴾ is in the sense of "with" (ma'a), as in their saying: "Every man with his property" (kullu rajulin wa ḍai'atahu). Just as it is permissible to stop at "every man and his property," so it is permissible to stop at His words ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾, because His words ﴿and what you worship﴾ take the place of the predicate, since its meaning is "So indeed you with what you worship." The meaning is: "So indeed you with your gods," that is, "So indeed you are their companions and associates, you will not abandon their worship." Then He said, exalted is He, ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against what you worship﴾, i.e., against what you worship, ﴿[anyone]﴾ by inciting or driving [them] to the path of temptation and misguidance, ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾, like you. Al-Hasan read *ṣālu al-jaḥīm* with a *ḍamma* on the *lam*. Its explanation is that it is a plural, and the dropping of its *waw* is due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn). If it is asked: "How does the plural fit with His words ﴿him who is﴾?" We say: *man* has a singular form but a plural meaning, so *huwa* is taken according to its form and *al-ṣālūn* according to its meaning.

**The second issue:** Our companions (the Ash'ari theologians) cited this verse as evidence that the whispering and seduction of Satan has no effect, and that the only effective cause is God's decree and determination. For God's words ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾ ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him﴾ are an explicit statement that their speech has no effect, and that the states of their objects of worship have no effect in bringing about temptation and misguidance. And His words ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾ mean: "except him who is such by God's judgment and decree." This is an explicit statement that what necessitates the occurrence of these events is God's judgment, exalted is He.

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz used to argue with this verse to establish this claim.

Al-Jubba'i said: The meaning is that those who worshipped the angels claimed that they were God's daughters, and they would not make anyone a disbeliever except one whom God knew would disbelieve. This indicates that whoever goes astray by the call of Satan would not have believed in God even if God had prevented Satan from calling him; otherwise, [God] would be preventing Satan. Thus it is established by this that every one who disobeys, nothing of the acts would have been correct for him.

The answer: The essential point of this argument is that the seduction of the devils of mankind and jinn has no effect. There is no dispute about this. But the way of the argument is that God explained that their speech has no effect on the occurrence of temptation, then He made an exception from it in His words ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾. Therefore it must be that what is meant by the occurrence of temptation is his being judged as "destined to burn in Hellfire," and this is an explicit statement that God's judgment of happiness and wretchedness is what effects the attainment of wretchedness and happiness.

Know that our companions established this argument by the well-known hadith that "Adam argued with Moses." The Qadi (said): This hadith has not been accepted by the scholars of tawhid, because it entails that no one should be blamed for any of the sins, for if Adam did not permit Moses to blame him for an act that God had written for him before creating him, then likewise every sinner [should not be blamed]. If this argument is valid for Adam, peace be upon him, then why did Moses, peace be upon him, say concerning the striking [of the Egyptian]: ﴿This is from the work of Satan; indeed, he is a misleading, manifest enemy﴾? And why did he say ﴿So I will never be a helper to the criminals﴾? And why did he blame Pharaoh and his soldiers for a matter that God had written against them? And it is among the strangest of their affairs that they declare the Qadariyya (those who deny predestination) to be disbelievers, while this hadith necessitates that Adam was a Qadari, so it is incumbent upon them to declare him a disbeliever. And how is it permissible, given the words of Adam and Eve, peace be upon them: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [Al-A'raf: 23], that he argue against Moses that there is no blame upon him, when that was written for him before he was created? This is the whole of the Qadi's speech.

It is said to him: Suppose you do not accept that report. Do you then reject this verse or not? For we have explained that the explicit wording of this verse indicates that the whisperings have no effect in this matter, since everything occurs by God's wisdom, exalted is He. And what indicates this are several aspects:

The first: If the disbeliever went astray because of the whispering of Satan, then if the misguidance of that Satan was caused by another Satan, an infinite regress of devils would follow, which is impossible. And if it ends at a misguidance that did not occur through a previous whispering, then that is what is sought.

The second: Every person wishes to attain for himself the correct belief and true religion, so the occurrence of its opposite indicates that this is not from him.

The third: Actions depend on motives, and the occurrence of motives is by God's creation, so all of it is from God, exalted is He.

The fourth: When God, exalted is He, required something by His wisdom, and its occurrence was known, then if that thing did not occur, it would necessitate that that judgment turn into a lie and that knowledge turn into ignorance, and that is impossible. As for the verses on which the Qadi relied, they are opposed by the verses indicating that everything is from God. The Qur'an is like a sea full of these verses. So the rational proofs we have mentioned remain sound. And God knows best.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾. The majority hold that they are the angels, who described themselves with exaggeration in servitude, for they line up for prayer and glorification. The purpose of this is to alert to the corruption of the view of those who say they are the children of God. This is because their extreme servitude indicates their acknowledgment of servitude. Know that this verse indicates three kinds of the attributes of the angels:

The first of them is His words ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾. This indicates that each one of them has a rank he does not exceed and a degree he does not go beyond. Those degrees are an allusion to their degrees in managing the bodies of this world and to their degrees in knowing God, exalted is He. As for their degrees in actions and activities, it is His words ﴿And indeed, we are those who stand in ranks﴾, meaning that they are standing in performing acts of obedience and in the stations of service and servitude. As for their degrees in knowledge, it is His words ﴿And indeed, we are those who glorify [Him]﴾, and glorification is the declaring of God free of what is not fitting for Him.

Know that His words ﴿And indeed, we are those who stand in ranks﴾ ﴿And indeed, we are those who glorify [Him]﴾ indicate restriction (al-hasr), and its meaning is that they are the ones who stand in the stations of servitude and no others, and that they are the ones who glorify and no others. This indicates that the acts of obedience and knowledge of humans, in relation to the acts of obedience and knowledge of the angels, are as nothing, such that this restriction would be valid. In sum, these three expressions indicate wondrous secrets of the attributes of the angels. So how is it permissible, given this restriction, to say that a human's rank approaches that of an angel, let alone to ask whether he is better than him or not?

* * *

As for His words ﴿And indeed, they were saying﴾ ﴿"If only we had a reminder from the former peoples﴾ ﴿we would surely be sincere servants of God"﴾, the meaning is that the polytheists of Quraysh and others used to say: ﴿"If only we had a reminder"﴾, that is, a book from the books of the former peoples to whom the Torah and the Gospel were sent, "we would have made our worship sincerely for God, and we would not have denied [it] as they denied." Then the Reminder came to them, which is the lord of reminders and the book that oversees all books, namely the Qur'an, and they disbelieved in it. A parallel to this verse is His words: ﴿But when a warner came to them, it increased them only in aversion﴾ [Fatir: 42]. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But they will soon know﴾, that is, they will soon know the consequence of this disbelief and denial.

If it is asked, "How can they lead them astray against God?" We say: they lead them astray against Him by their misguidance of them, from your saying "Fulan seduced Fulan against Fulan's wife" (fatana Fulan 'ala Fulan imra'atahu), just as you say "he corrupted her against him" (af sadaha 'alayhi).

The second possibility: the *waw* in His words ﴿and what you worship﴾ is in the sense of "with" (ma'a), as in their saying: "Every man with his property" (kullu rajulin wa ḍai'atahu). Just as it is permissible to stop at "every man and his property," so it is permissible to stop at His words ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾, because His words ﴿and what you worship﴾ take the place of the predicate, since its meaning is "So indeed you with what you worship." Then He said, exalted is He, ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against what you worship﴾, i.e., against what you worship, ﴿[anyone]﴾ by inciting or driving [them] to the path of temptation and misguidance, ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾, like you. Al-Hasan read *ṣālu al-jaḥīm* with a *ḍamma* on the *lam*. Its explanation is that it is a plural, and the dropping of its *waw* is due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn). If it is asked: "How does the plural fit with His words ﴿him who is﴾?" We say: *man* has a singular form but a plural meaning, so *huwa* is taken according to its form and *al-ṣālūn* according to its meaning.

**The second issue:** Our companions (the Ash'ari theologians) cited this verse as evidence that the whispering and seduction of Satan has no effect, and that the only effective cause is God's decree and determination. For God's words ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾ ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him﴾ are an explicit statement that their speech has no effect, and that the states of their objects of worship have no effect in bringing about temptation and misguidance. And His words ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾ mean: "except him who is such by God's judgment and decree." This is an explicit statement that what necessitates the occurrence of these events is God's judgment, exalted is He.

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz used to argue with this verse to establish this claim.

Al-Jubba'i said: The meaning is that those who worshipped the angels claimed that they were God's daughters, and they would not make anyone a disbeliever except one whom God knew would disbelieve. This indicates that whoever goes astray by the call of Satan would not have believed in God even if God had prevented Satan from calling him; otherwise, [God] would be preventing Satan. The answer: The essential point of this argument is that the seduction of the devils of mankind and jinn has no effect. There is no dispute about this. But the way of the argument is that God explained that their speech has no effect on the occurrence of temptation, then He made an exception from it in His words ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾. Therefore it must be that what is meant by the occurrence of temptation is his being judged as "destined to burn in Hellfire," and this is an explicit statement that God's judgment of happiness and wretchedness is what effects the attainment of wretchedness and happiness.

Know that our companions established this argument by the well-known hadith that "Adam argued with Moses." The Qadi (said): This hadith has not been accepted by the scholars of tawhid, because it entails that no one should be blamed for any of the sins, for if Adam did not permit Moses to blame him for an act that God had written for him before creating him, then likewise every sinner [should not be blamed]. And it is among the strangest of their affairs that they declare the Qadariyya (those who deny predestination) to be disbelievers, while this hadith necessitates that Adam was a Qadari, so it is incumbent upon them to declare him a disbeliever. And how is it permissible, given the words of Adam and Eve, peace be upon them: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [Al-A'raf: 23], that he argue against Moses that there is no blame upon him, when that was written for him before he was created? For we have explained that the explicit wording of this verse indicates that the whisperings have no effect in this matter, since everything occurs by God's wisdom, exalted is He. And what indicates this are several aspects:

The first: If the disbeliever went astray because of the whispering of Satan, then if the misguidance of that Satan was caused by another Satan, an infinite regress of devils would follow, which is impossible. The third: Actions depend on motives, and the occurrence of motives is by God's creation, so all of it is from God, exalted is He.

The fourth: When God, exalted is He, required something by His wisdom, and its occurrence was known, then if that thing did not occur, it would necessitate that that judgment turn into a lie and that knowledge turn into ignorance, and that is impossible. As for the verses on which the Qadi relied, they are opposed by the verses indicating that everything is from God. The Qur'an is like a sea full of these verses. So the rational proofs we have mentioned remain sound. And God knows best.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 37, verses 164–172**

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾ ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him﴾ ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾ ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾ ﴿And indeed, we are those who stand in ranks﴾ ﴿And indeed, we are those who glorify [Him]﴾ ﴿And indeed, they were saying﴾ ﴿"If only we had a reminder from the former peoples﴾ ﴿we would surely be sincere servants of God"﴾ ﴿But they disbelieved in it, so they will soon know.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Know that when God, exalted is He, mentioned the proofs against the corrupt doctrine of the disbelievers, He followed it with something that alerts to the fact that these disbelievers have no power to lead anyone astray unless God's judgment concerning him has already preceded, [determining] his punishment and his falling into the Fire. The author of *al-Kashshaf* (Zamakhshari's commentary) mentioned two opinions concerning God's words ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾ ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him﴾:

The first: the pronoun in ﴿against Him﴾ refers to God, the Mighty and Majestic. Its meaning is: "So indeed you and your objects of worship, you all together cannot lead astray against God anyone except the companions of the Fire, those whose being among the people of the Fire was already decreed in God's knowledge." If it is asked, "How can they lead them astray against God?" We say: they lead them astray against Him by their misguidance of them, from your saying "Fulan seduced Fulan against Fulan's wife" (fatana Fulan 'ala Fulan imra'atahu), just as you say "he corrupted her against him" (af sadaha 'alayhi).

The second possibility: the *waw* in His words ﴿and what you worship﴾ is in the sense of "with" (ma'a), as in their saying: "Every man with his property" (kullu rajulin wa ḍai'atahu). Just as it is permissible to stop at "every man and his property," so it is permissible to stop at His words ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾, because His words ﴿and what you worship﴾ take the place of the predicate, since its meaning is "So indeed you with what you worship." The meaning is: "So indeed you with your gods," that is, "So indeed you are their companions and associates, you will not abandon their worship." Then He said, exalted is He, ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against what you worship﴾, i.e., against what you worship, ﴿[anyone]﴾ by inciting or driving [them] to the path of temptation and misguidance, ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾, like you. Al-Hasan read *ṣālu al-jaḥīm* with a *ḍamma* on the *lam*. Its explanation is that it is a plural, and the dropping of its *waw* is due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn). If it is asked: "How does the plural fit with His words ﴿him who is﴾?" We say: *man* has a singular form but a plural meaning, so *huwa* is taken according to its form and *al-ṣālūn* according to its meaning.

**The second issue:** Our companions (the Ash'ari theologians) cited this verse as evidence that the whispering and seduction of Satan has no effect, and that the only effective cause is God's decree and determination. For God's words ﴿So indeed you and what you worship﴾ ﴿cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him﴾ are an explicit statement that their speech has no effect, and that the states of their objects of worship have no effect in bringing about temptation and misguidance. And His words ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾ mean: "except him who is such by God's judgment and decree." This is an explicit statement that what necessitates the occurrence of these events is God's judgment, exalted is He.

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz used to argue with this verse to establish this claim.

Al-Jubba'i said: The meaning is that those who worshipped the angels claimed that they were God's daughters, and they would not make anyone a disbeliever except one whom God knew would disbelieve. This indicates that whoever goes astray by the call of Satan would not have believed in God even if God had prevented Satan from calling him; otherwise, [God] would be preventing Satan. Thus it is established by this that every one who disobeys, nothing of the acts would have been correct for him.

The answer: The essential point of this argument is that the seduction of the devils of mankind and jinn has no effect. There is no dispute about this. But the way of the argument is that God explained that their speech has no effect on the occurrence of temptation, then He made an exception from it in His words ﴿except him who is destined to burn in Hellfire﴾. Therefore it must be that what is meant by the occurrence of temptation is his being judged as "destined to burn in Hellfire," and this is an explicit statement that God's judgment of happiness and wretchedness is what effects the attainment of wretchedness and happiness.

Know that our companions established this argument by the well-known hadith that "Adam argued with Moses." The Qadi (said): This hadith has not been accepted by the scholars of tawhid, because it entails that no one should be blamed for any of the sins, for if Adam did not permit Moses to blame him for an act that God had written for him before creating him, then likewise every sinner [should not be blamed]. If this argument is valid for Adam, peace be upon him, then why did Moses, peace be upon him, say concerning the striking [of the Egyptian]: ﴿This is from the work of Satan; indeed, he is a misleading, manifest enemy﴾? And why did he say ﴿So I will never be a helper to the criminals﴾? And why did he blame Pharaoh and his soldiers for a matter that God had written against them? And it is among the strangest of their affairs that they declare the Qadariyya (those who deny predestination) to be disbelievers, while this hadith necessitates that Adam was a Qadari, so it is incumbent upon them to declare him a disbeliever. And how is it permissible, given the words of Adam and Eve, peace be upon them: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [Al-A'raf: 23], that he argue against Moses that there is no blame upon him, when that was written for him before he was created? This is the whole of the Qadi's speech.

It is said to him: Suppose you do not accept that report. Do you then reject this verse or not? For we have explained that the explicit wording of this verse indicates that the whisperings have no effect in this matter, since everything occurs by God's wisdom, exalted is He. And what indicates this are several aspects:

The first: If the disbeliever went astray because of the whispering of Satan, then if the misguidance of that Satan was caused by another Satan, an infinite regress of devils would follow, which is impossible. And if it ends at a misguidance that did not occur through a previous whispering, then that is what is sought.

The second: Every person wishes to attain for himself the correct belief and true religion, so the occurrence of its opposite indicates that this is not from him.

The third: Actions depend on motives, and the occurrence of motives is by God's creation, so all of it is from God, exalted is He.

As for the verses on which the Qadi relied, they are opposed by the verses indicating that everything is from God. The Qur'an is like a sea full of these verses. So the rational proofs we have mentioned remain sound. And God knows best.

﴿And Our word had already been passed to Our servants, the messengers﴾ ﴿that they would surely be helped﴾ ﴿and that Our soldiers would surely be the victors﴾ ﴿So turn away from them for a while﴾ ﴿and watch them, for they will soon see﴾ ﴿Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ ﴿But when it descends upon their courtyard, evil is the morning of those who were warned﴾ ﴿So turn away from them for a while﴾ ﴿and watch, for they will soon see﴾ ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe﴾ ﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾ ﴿And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾.

[p. 150]
Know that when He (exalted is He) threatened the disbelievers with His words, ﴿so they will soon know﴾, meaning the outcome of their disbelief, He followed it with what strengthens the heart of the Messenger (ﷺ), saying: ﴿And Our word had already been passed to Our servants, the messengers﴾ ﴿that they would surely be helped﴾ ﴿and that Our soldiers would surely be the victors﴾. Thus He clarified that His promise of support had already preceded. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾. Also, good is decreed essentially (bi'l-dhat) and evil is decreed incidentally (bi'l-'arad), and what is essential is stronger than what is incidental. As for victory and triumph, they may come through the strength of proof, may come through dominion and control, and may come through permanence and steadfastness. So the believer, even if he is overcome at some times because of the weakness of worldly conditions, is still the victor. It does not follow from this verse that some prophets were killed or that many believers were defeated, since the verse concerns the ultimate outcome.

Then He said to His Messenger, after having informed him of what preceded: ﴿So turn away from them for a while﴾. The meaning is to abandon fighting them and to trust in what We have promised them, until a time when they enjoy themselves, after which regret and remorse will befall them. The commentators differed: it was said the intended time is the Day of Badr; it was said, until the conquest of Mecca; and it was said, until the Day of Resurrection.

Then He said: ﴿and watch them, for they will soon see﴾. The meaning is: watch them, and what will be decreed against them of killing and captivity in this world and of punishment in the Hereafter, while they will soon see you with what has been ordained for you of victory and support in this world and of great reward in the Hereafter. The sense of the matter being witnessed by their eyes in the awaited and promised state is the indication that it is certainly coming and will surely occur, and that its occurrence is near, as if it were before your eyes. His saying ﴿for they will soon see﴾ is for threat and warning.

Then He said: ﴿Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ The meaning is that the Messenger (peace be upon him) used to threaten them with punishment, and since they had seen nothing, they would hasten the descent of that punishment mockingly. So God (exalted is He) clarified that this hastening is ignorance, because for everything in God's acts there is a specific time that neither advances nor delays. Therefore, seeking its occurrence before that time comes is ignorance.

Then God (exalted is He) said, describing the punishment they hasten: ﴿But when it descends upon their courtyard﴾, that is, this punishment, ﴿evil is the morning of those who were warned﴾. This expression for these meanings occurred because they used to come upon (the enemy) at the time of morning as a habit, so mention of that time was made a metonym (kinayah) for that action.

Then God repeated His words: ﴿So turn away from them for a while﴾ ﴿and watch, for they will soon see﴾. It was said that the meaning of this phrase in the earlier instance is the conditions of this world, and in this instance the conditions of the Resurrection; on this reading the repetition is not redundant. It was also said that the purpose of the repetition is to intensify the threat and the awe-inspiring warning.

Then He (exalted is He) concluded the surah with a noble conclusion comprehensive of all lofty aims, because the most important of matters for the intelligent person is knowing three states.

The first of them: knowing the God of the world to the extent of human capacity. The highest that can be known of God's attributes is of three kinds:

One: His transcendence and sanctification above everything unfitting to divine attributes, and this is the word ﴿Glory be﴾.

Second: describing Him with everything fitting to divine attributes, and this is His saying ﴿the Lord of might﴾. For lordship (rububiyyah, the sustaining and nurturing of creation) points to nurture, which indicates perfect wisdom, while mercy and might point to perfect power.

Third: His being exalted in divinity above partners and equals. His saying ﴿the Lord of might﴾ indicates that He is capable of all occurrences, because the definite article in ﴿might﴾ (al-'izzah) conveys totality. When everything is His possession and His property, nothing remains for anyone else. Thus it is established that His saying ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe﴾ is a statement containing the highest degrees and most perfect limits in knowing the God of the world.

The second of the intelligent person's concerns: that he know how he should treat himself and treat creation in this worldly life.

Know that most of creation is deficient, and they must have one who perfects them, a guide who guides them, and a leader who leads them. This is none other than the prophets, upon them be prayers and peace. The self-evident nature of innate disposition (fitrah) testifies that the deficient must follow the perfect. He drew attention to this point with His saying ﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾, because this expression indicates that they surpassed others in the perfection fitting for humans.

[p. 151]
Others, and there is no doubt that everyone else must follow them.

The third of the intelligent person's concerns: that he know what his condition will be after death.

Know that knowing this state before death is difficult, so reliance in it is upon one point, namely that the God of the world is self-sufficient (ghani) and merciful (rahim), and the self-sufficient and merciful does not punish. He drew attention to this point with His saying ﴿And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾. This is because the entitlement to praise is only obtained through great bounty; thus by this He clarified that He is a bestower, and the evident fact that He is self-sufficient of the worlds. From this description, what predominates of Him is mercy, grace and generosity. So this point alerts to the soundness of one's condition after death.

From what we have mentioned, it becomes clear that this conclusion is like a shell containing pearls nobler than the glittering stars. We ask God, glory be to Him and exalted is He, for a good ending, and well-being in this world and the Hereafter.
